title: MSYS dollar-escape broke mkdir and wrote captures to WSL root
body: First probe used \$T inside a double-quoted wsl bash -c string; the escape collapsed, mkdir got no operand, and the six capture files landed at /apt_installed.txt-style absolute paths in the WSL root. Fix: create the dir in its own wsl call, then mv the files in. Lesson: one filesystem mutation per wsl invocation, verify the landing path before trusting a capture.

title: Excluding REMOVE-candidates from users collapsed dependency chains
body: First classifier dropped users that were themselves REMOVE-bound; sherlock-project (orphan CLI) went REMOVE and dragged stem (required only by sherlock) with it, then --check correctly failed on stem having reverse deps. Fix: fixed-point KEEP from rooted sets (imported, baseline, lane tools, self, managed, runtime) with no exclusion; dead chains fall out as REMOVE with their top named. The gate caught the exact defect it was built for.

title: Reverse-dep map keys carried version markers and underscores
body: The WSL one-liner keyed requirements by r.split()[0], so keys like jupyter-server<3,>=1.8 kept their version pins and aiohttp_socks never matched dist aiohttp-socks. 1,942 of 2,192 keys missed the in-env set. Fix: PEP 503 normalization (lowercase, [-_.] to hyphen, strip markers/extras/version) applied on load in the tool, plus self-edge drops. Lesson: normalize at the consumer, never trust the producer's key shape.

title: Path.write_text CRLF-poisoned the generated shrink scripts
body: The emitted .sh files carried CRLF because write_text translates newlines on Windows; bash died on set -u with a carriage-return option error. Fix: write_lf() helper using open(path, w, newline=\n) for all generated scripts. Lesson: every generated executable artifact needs a newline contract, and the first run of a generated script is its test.

title: Triple-nested bash quoting silently emptied the verify loop variable
body: The dpkg/pip absent-check passed through Git Bash, wsl.exe, and two bash -c layers; the loop variable arrived empty and dpkg -l with no args matched everything, printing four STILL PRESENT rows with blank names. Fix: write the verifier to a script file with printf and execute the file -- no inline nesting. Lesson: beyond two quoting layers, always use a file.

title: pygame dist was imported only by the dead module itself
body: The import scan counted import pygame inside src/azazael_pygame.py as a tree consumer of the pygame dist, but nothing imports azazael_pygame on either checkout (Windows 2026-10-11 measure plus WSL grep today: only docs/reports/pycache mention it). Fix: PIP_OVERRIDES table for dists whose sole importer is a dead module. Lesson: a dist-level scan must ask who imports the importer.

title: XPU runtime coupling is invisible to Requires-Dist
body: torch 2.14.1+xpu dlopens the intel/mkl/oneapi shared libraries without declaring them, so the fixed-point classifier marked the whole XPU stack a dead chain. Removing it would have broken the engineered replacement. Fix: RUNTIME protection set owned by device.py's XPU preference plus the /opt+15t sidecar evidence. Lesson: metadata answers declared coupling only; runtime coupling needs a named owner.

title: Project's own installed dists looked like orphans
body: azazael-*, eve-unleashed, and worm-manifest are pip-installed copies of this repo; nothing imports them as libraries and nothing requires them, so the classifier queued them for removal -- which would strand console scripts with no import error. Fix: SELF recognition (azazael prefix + exact names) rooted as self-install, enforced by --check. Lesson: the project's own artifacts are the first thing a shrink tool must learn not to eat.

title: BM Ubuntu verdicts are derived, never present them as probed
body: BM is dual-boot with Windows running, so no live probe is possible from here; its package surface is the runbook's prescribed set plus stock Ubuntu. The manifest's BM section is therefore a path-forward plan (post-shrink allowlist, interpreter convergence) and is labeled derived in two places, with the execution record restating the limit. Lesson: an unreachable host contributes a plan, never a measurement.

title: pip uninstalled files owned by apt packages on Kali
body: Classifier without location-awareness marked 266 SYSTEM-owned pip-visible dists as orphans; pip uninstall deleted files out from under 80 python3-* apt packages (measured via dpkg -V missing counts, e.g. python3-dnslib 22 missing). Repaired with apt-get install --reinstall over all 80 damaged; dpkg -V clean after (0 missing), apt-get check and dpkg --audit clean.

title: Only ENV-located dists are pip candidates
body: Hardened tools/env_supersede.py with locations.json awareness: dists installed under the OS dist-packages (/usr/lib/python3) are APT-OWNED keep rows (apt surface only, never pip-touched); only ENV-located dists (/usr/local, .local) enter REMOVE candidacy. Missing location data falls back to legacy behavior; freeze comment (-e/#) lines are now skipped after '#' and 'e' parsed as orphan dists.

title: Kali steady state remove=0 both managers
body: Kali final: apt 4379->4349 installed (-30: 19 named REMOVE + 11 autoremove), pip freeze 1028->995 (277 env-owned dists removed; delta smaller because apt-reinstall restored deleted apt dist-infos). Classifier post-state: pip keep=990 remove=0, apt remove=0 missing=19, dpkg -V clean. Recon smoke: bloodhound-python --help OK, nxc 1.5.1 OK, shodan/holehe/maigret/sherlock_project/dns imports OK.

title: Bare import bloodhound hangs; CLI unaffected; pre-existing
body: Bare 'import bloodhound' hangs on BOTH copies including the pristine apt-reinstalled one, while bloodhound-python --help works and all leaf deps (ldap3, neo4j, impacket, dns, crypto) import cleanly. Hang reproduces with factory-pristine files, so it predates this shrink and is out of scope; recorded here so the next session does not re-litigate it.

title: WSL probes must be file-based with exact bytes
body: Four probe failures in one session from shell-quoting layers: inline -c with inner quotes silently produced empty files, exec-prefix eats trailing echo, MSYS2 mangles bare interpreter paths, and 9p write-visibility races. Discipline that held: generate all WSL scripts via write_file (exact bytes), execute via 'wsl -d <d> -- bash -c "exec <script-path>"', never parse output through head-masked exit codes.

title: Observability dashboard + BM runbook shipped
body: tools/supersede_dashboard.py reads the committed Ubuntu+Kali manifests (numbers carry manifest provenance) and emits docs/supersede_dashboard.html: estate before/after, REMOVE verdicts, curated KEEP do-not-touch lists, execution records, verify commands, BM checklist. docs/BM_SUPERSEDE_RUNBOOK.md gives BM the capture-classify-review-execute-verify-record replay with the locations.json precondition that would have prevented the Kali massacre.
